verses.text: It was now two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for a sly way to arrest Jesus and kill him.
"But not during the feast," they said, "or the people may start a riot."

Jesus was in Bethany, eating at the house of a man known as Simon the Leper. A woman came with a jar made of white stone. It was full of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar open and poured the perfume on his head.
Some of the people there were angry. They said to each other, "Why waste this perfume?
It could have been sold for more than a year's wages, and the money given to poor people." And they spoke harshly to her.
"Leave her alone," said Jesus. "Why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
You will always have poor people with you, and you can help them any time you want. But you will not always have me.
She did what she could. She poured perfume on my body ahead of time to get it ready to be buried.
I tell you for certain, wherever the good news is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, so that people will remember her."
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
They were happy to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas watched for a good time to hand Jesus over.
On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the day when the Passover lamb was killed, Jesus' followers asked him, "Where do you want us to go and prepare the Passover meal for you?"
So he sent two of his followers and told them, "Go into the city. A man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
Say to the owner of the house he goes into, 'The Teacher asks, "Where is my guest room, where I can eat the Passover with my followers?"'
He will show you a large upstairs room, with everything ready. Prepare for us there."
The followers left and went into the city. They found things just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus arrived with the twelve.
While they were at the table eating, Jesus said, "I tell you for certain, one of you will hand me over to my enemies. He is eating with me."
They became very sad. One by one they said to him, "Surely you do not mean me?"
"It is one of the twelve," Jesus replied. "It is the one who dips bread into the bowl with me.
The Son of Man will go just as it is written about him. But how terrible it will be for the one who hands over the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had never been born."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread. He gave thanks and broke it. He gave it to his followers and said, "Take it. This is my body."
Then he took the cup. He gave thanks and handed it to them, and they all drank from it.
"This is my blood of the new covenant," he said to them. "It is poured out for many people.
I tell you for certain, I will not drink wine again until the day I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus told them, "All of you will turn away from me tonight. It is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter said, "Even if all the others turn away, I will not."
"I tell you for certain," Jesus answered, "today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you yourself will say three times that you do not know me."
But Peter kept saying firmly, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I do not know you." And all the others said the same.
They went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to his followers, "Sit here while I pray."
He took Peter, James and John along with him. He began to be very upset and troubled.
"My soul is so full of sorrow that I feel as if I am dying," he said to them. "Stay here and keep watch."
He went a little further. Then he fell to the ground and prayed that, if possible, this time of suffering might pass him by.
"Abba, Father," he said, "everything is possible for you. Take this cup of suffering away from me. But let what you want be done, not what I want."
Then he came back to his followers and found them sleeping. "Simon," he said to Peter, "are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?
Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."
Once more Jesus went away and prayed the same thing.
Then he came back and again found them sleeping, because their eyes were very heavy. They did not know what to say to him.
He came back the third time and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The time has come. Look, the Son of Man is about to be handed over to sinners.
Get up! Let us go! Here comes the one who is handing me over!"
Just as Jesus was speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, appeared. With him was a crowd carrying swords and clubs. The chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders had sent them.
Judas, the one who was handing Jesus over, had given them a signal. "The one I kiss is the man," he had said. "Arrest him and take him away under guard."
So Judas went to Jesus straight away. "Rabbi!" he said, and kissed him.
The men grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
Then one of the people standing nearby pulled out his sword. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
"Am I leading a revolt against you," said Jesus, "that you have come out with swords and clubs to capture me?
Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But the Scriptures must come true."
Then all his followers left him and ran away.
A young man was following Jesus. He was wearing nothing but a linen cloth. When the crowd grabbed him,
he ran away naked, leaving the linen cloth behind.
They took Jesus to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders and the teachers of the law gathered there.
Peter followed Jesus from a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. There he sat with the guards and warmed himself at the fire.
The chief priests and the whole Council were looking for something to use against Jesus so that they could put him to death. But they did not find anything.
Many people told lies about him, but their stories did not agree.
Then some stood up and told this lie about him:
"We heard him say, 'I will destroy this temple made by people. In three days I will build another temple, not made by people.'"
But even then their stories did not agree.
Then the high priest stood up in front of them all. He asked Jesus, "Are you not going to answer? What are these charges that these men are bringing against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest asked him, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
"I am," said Jesus. "And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of the Mighty One. You will see him coming on the clouds of heaven."
The high priest tore his clothes. "Why do we need any more witnesses?" he asked.
"You have heard him insult God. What do you think?" They all said he was guilty and should be put to death.
Then some of them began to spit at him. They covered his face and hit him with their fists. They said, "Prophesy!" And the guards took him and beat him.
Peter was below in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came by.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him. "You also were with that man from Nazareth, Jesus," she said.
But Peter said it was not true. "I do not know or understand what you are talking about," he said. Then he went out into the entrance, and a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him there. She said again to the people standing around, "This man is one of them."
Again he said it was not true. A little later, the people standing near Peter said to him, "You must be one of them. You are from Galilee."
Then Peter began to call down curses on himself, and he swore to them, "I do not know this man you are talking about!"

Straight away the rooster crowed the second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: "Before the rooster crows twice, you will say three times that you do not know me." And he broke down and cried.
